elements.quote: The finding of this SRMA showed that the pooled prevalence of surgical site infection after cesarean section in Ethiopia was 11.13% (95% CI: 9.29, 12.97%), and there is significant heterogeneity between the studies as evidenced by the Cochrane heterogeneity index (I 2 = 86.80%), P = 0.00.
elements.reason: Results for pooled prevalence meta-analysis and heterogeneity are reported, but sensitivity analysis results are mentioned without detailed reporting in retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: The pooled estimate of SSI in Ethiopia was 11.13% (95%CI, 9.29-12.97%). Prolonged labor (AOR = 3.16, 95% CI; (2.14-4.68)), chorioamnionitis (AOR = 4.26, 95% CI; (1.99-8.91)), prolonged PROM (AOR = 3.80, 95% CI; (2.51-5.62)), repeated vaginal examination (AOR = 3.80, 95% CI; (2.45-5.88)), decreased hemoglobin level (AOR = 4.57, 95%CI; (3.16-6.60)), vertical skin incision (AOR = 3.09, 95% CI; (2.04-4.67)) and general anesthesia (AOR = 1.82, 95% CI (1.21-2.75)) are significantly associated with SSI after cesarean section in Ethiopia.
elements.reason: Summary estimates and 95% confidence intervals are reported for both prevalence and predictor meta-analyses.

elements.quote: there is significant heterogeneity between the studies as evidenced by the Cochrane heterogeneity index (I 2 = 86.80%), P = 0.00.
elements.reason: Heterogeneity measures (I², p-value) are reported for the prevalence meta-analysis, but not explicitly for the predictor meta-analysis in retrieved evidence.
Subgroup analysis results with effect sizes and confidence intervals are reported in the table, but sensitivity analysis results are not detailed in retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: there is significant heterogeneity between the studies as evidenced by the Cochrane heterogeneity index (I 2 = 86.80%), P = 0.00.
elements.reason: Statistics (I², p-value) and a question-consistent interpretation (significant heterogeneity) are provided for heterogeneity assessment.

elements.quote: Prolonged labor (AOR = 3.16, 95% CI; (2.14-4.68)), ... are significantly associated with SSI after cesarean section in Ethiopia.
elements.reason: Direction of effect is described as increased odds (AOR > 1) for predictors associated with SSI.
